name: NJ-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's 14-point Republican partisan lean anchors the race
Smith's four-decade incumbency and durable personal brand
Large fundraising gap: $592k raised and $488k banked vs. $93k and $9k for Peace
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 97% to win
model.rationale: The district's 14-point Republican lean, Smith's four decades of incumbency, and his six-to-one fundraising advantage over Peace make an upset highly improbable; markets and fundamentals converge on a decisive Republican win even in a Democratic-leaning national environment.
model.watch: A severe late national wave toward Democrats combined with heavy outside spending could narrow the margin, though Smith has held this seat comfortably even in hostile cycles.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 4th District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about 14 points toward the GOP. Chris Smith, first elected in 1980, is among the longest-serving members of the House and has built a durable record of constituent service. He enters the general election with a major financial edge, roughly $592,000 raised and $488,000 on hand, while Democrat Rachel Peace has raised about $93,000 and ended the period with under $10,000 in the bank.

No public polling of the race is available, and prediction markets give Smith about a 97 percent chance of holding the seat. Even with a national climate tilted toward Democrats, the district's lean, Smith's incumbency, and the money gap point to a decisive Republican victory, with Peace needing an exceptional and unexpected surge to become competitive.
